title: Normalized source-open comparison for differential transitivity
statement: Let X,Y,S be schemes [def-pc-scheme], h:X→Y and g:Y→S morphisms, and q:Ω_{X/S}→Ω_{X/Y} a morphism of O_X-modules [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] sending da to da on every source open. Use the canonical first arrow u of [def-a1-relative-differentials-pullback-map] and tensor module pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback]. For each source open O⊆X, j:O→X, there exist an isomorphism e:(h*Ω_{Y/S})|_O≅(hj)*Ω_{Y/S} and a map q_O:Ω_{O/S}→Ω_{O/Y}. The isomorphism takes every restriction of an actual pulled-back db section to the actual pulled-back db for hj. The squares for u and q, with the specified relativeDifferentialsRestrictIso and the associativity congruence for j,h,g, commute. Finally q_O(da)=da on every open of O. This statement asserts only the restriction comparison and its normalization, not exactness.

proof.text: Let j:O→X be the source-open inclusion. Restriction is the pullback for j. Compose its restriction adjunction with the normalized tensor pullback adjunction for h, and compare with the normalized tensor pullback adjunction for j≫h, using the canonical composition isomorphism of pushforwards. Uniqueness of left adjoints constructs e. Its unit identity says on every local section that e carries the restricted tensor unit to the tensor unit for j≫h; apply this to db to obtain the required normalization.

Use the universal derivation for j≫h as a derivation relative to j≫(h≫g), and use the universal property to construct q_O with da↦da. For the second square, apply the restriction adjunction Hom equivalence and then the differential universal-property Hom equivalence; naturality of the first reduces both sides on da to d(j♯a), using q(da)=da and q_O(da)=da. For the first square, apply the composite of the tensor and restriction adjunctions and then the universal-property Hom equivalence for Ω_{Y/S}. The left-adjoint uniqueness identity converts the route through e to the tensor adjunction for j≫h. On db the two sides are d(j♯h♯b), by the tensor-unit formulas, the defining canonical first-arrow formulas, and the source-restriction derivation formula. Equality induction proves that the associativity congruence also preserves differentials. Injectivity of the Hom equivalences proves both squares as sheaf morphism equalities, including empty opens. No localization or exactness assertion is needed for this comparison.

theorem relativeDifferentials_transitivity_open
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (h : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (q : (h ≫ g).relativeDifferentials ⟶ h.relativeDifferentials)
    (hq : ∀ (O : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, O)),
      q.app O ((h ≫ g).relativeDifferentialsDerivation.d (X := op O) a) =
        h.relativeDifferentialsDerivation.d (X := op O) a) :
      (∀ O : X.Opens,
        ∃ (e : ((Modules.tensorPullback h).obj g.relativeDifferentials).restrict O.ι ≅
              (Modules.tensorPullback (O.ι ≫ h)).obj g.relativeDifferentials)
          (qO : (O.ι ≫ (h ≫ g)).relativeDifferentials ⟶ (O.ι ≫ h).relativeDifferentials),
          (∀ (V : Y.Opens) (b : Γ(Y, V)),
            e.hom.app (O.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (h ⁻¹ᵁ V))
              (((Modules.tensorPullback h).obj g.relativeDifferentials).presheaf.map
                (homOfLE (O.ι.image_preimage_le (h ⁻¹ᵁ V))).op
                  (g.relativeDifferentialsPullbackGenerator h V b)) =
              g.relativeDifferentialsPullbackGenerator (O.ι ≫ h) V b) ∧
          (Modules.restrictFunctor O.ι).map (g.relativeDifferentialsPullbackMap h) ≫
              ((h ≫ g).relativeDifferentialsRestrictIso O.ι).hom =
            e.hom ≫ g.relativeDifferentialsPullbackMap (O.ι ≫ h) ≫
              (relativeDifferentialsCongr _ (Category.assoc O.ι h g)).hom ∧
          (Modules.restrictFunctor O.ι).map q ≫
              (h.relativeDifferentialsRestrictIso O.ι).hom =
            ((h ≫ g).relativeDifferentialsRestrictIso O.ι).hom ≫ qO ∧
          (∀ (T : O.toScheme.Opens) (a : Γ(O.toScheme, T)),
            qO.app T ((O.ι ≫ (h ≫ g)).relativeDifferentialsDerivation.d (X := op T) a) =
              (O.ι ≫ h).relativeDifferentialsDerivation.d (X := op T) a))
